story: GraphBrew is an explicit composition framework with a faster, lower-cost GORDER-quality configuration and a separate mapping-construction optimization. Rabbit remains the practical low-overhead Pareto point, not a GraphBrew end-to-end victory.

methodology.kernel_ratio: Comparator median kernel time divided by GraphBrew median kernel time; values above one favor GraphBrew.
methodology.mapping_ratio: GraphBrew complete mapping time divided by comparator complete mapping time; values below one favor GraphBrew.
methodology.end_to_end: Complete mapping cost plus reuse multiplied by kernel time.
methodology.mandatory_baseline: ORIGINAL is required whenever a low-reuse or amortization claim is evaluated.
methodology.invalidated_data: Performance rows collected under inherited SCHED_IDLE/nice 19 are excluded. Their semantic verification rows remain verification evidence only.

quality_arm.name: LeidenGVE-SizeDesc-LocalGorder8
quality_arm.scope: Fresh semantics-v4 confirmation; 11 graphs, 7 kernels, 77 cells.
quality_arm.caveat: The defensible performance claim is versus GORDER_csr: GraphBrew is faster in kernel GM, maps 24.8% cheaper, and wins end to end from reuse one. The 4% Rabbit per-cell GM is driven by Afforest CC, disappears without CC, requires 17-19x mapping cost, and never becomes a summed-seconds win.

compact_and_emit.name: Compact-and-Emit
compact_and_emit.mechanism: Compact active one-pass community IDs and emit final IDs during BFS, eliminating sparse label-slot scheduling and the final assignment sweep.
compact_and_emit.caveat: The mandatory ORIGINAL audit found no low-reuse region that beats both doing nothing and Rabbit. Compact-and-Emit is a construction-cost contribution, not a balanced ordering claim.

composition_atlas.scope: Nine complete Rabbit-free GraphBrew arms on the historical 11-by-7 matrix.
composition_atlas.caveat: The atlas establishes compositional expressiveness: eight arms win cells and the cell oracle is 1.122x faster than the best fixed GraphBrew arm. It does not establish graph-type generalization: six of seven types are singletons and the held-out family/kernel policy reaches only 0.911x.

rejected_claims.claim: GraphBrew has a Rabbit-cost-balanced arm that also beats ORIGINAL.
rejected_claims.reason: Every cheap candidate failed the mandatory ORIGINAL/Rabbit overlap gate.

rejected_claims.claim: The Rabbit-fallback low-reuse policy is the paper contribution.
rejected_claims.reason: It is a competitor-backed diagnostic, omits selector feature time in its public accounting, and does not establish a Rabbit-free GraphBrew system.

rejected_claims.claim: The current composition library supports a graph-held-out adaptive generator.
rejected_claims.reason: The corrected graph-held-out policy reaches only 0.907x against the fastest comparator.

rejected_claims.claim: CC-SV lower-label portal layouts are promoted.
rejected_claims.reason: Frozen variants reduced work on selected graphs but failed locality, compression-work, or mapping-equivalence gates; all production hooks were removed.
